task.instruction: Respond to regional clinic leads by designing a common allocation rule for the limited vaccine shipment. Define the eligibility threshold and which local delivery adaptations remain permissible.
hardConstraints: Use only claims supported by the supplied documents and prior records.
Cite the decision evidence with [doc-03] and [doc-05].
The statutory eligibility order cannot vary by clinic; each clinic must reserve second doses already promised.
Separate observed facts, interpretation, and recommendation.

documents.title: Shipment and second-dose obligations
documents.content: The shipment contains 1,200 doses. Clinics must reserve 380 for documented second doses, leaving 820 first doses.

documents.title: Clinic parking changes
documents.content: South clinic parking is reduced during resurfacing. A temporary drop-off lane is available.

documents.title: Statutory priority order
documents.content: First doses must proceed through categories 1, 2, then 3. Clinics may change appointment channel and session hours but cannot reorder eligibility.

documents.title: Clinic lead requests
documents.content: North requests walk-ins for category 2; South requests priority for local teachers in category 3; East requests evening appointments because 41% of category 1 has not responded.

documents.title: Eligible residents and uptake
documents.content: Unserved category 1: North 190, South 140, East 230. Unserved category 2: North 180, South 150, East 210. Confirmed appointments total 610.

target_a.content:
Situation: A food bank is redesigning appointment reminders across four neighborhoods.
Shared facts [history-03-01-fact]: Language mix and phone access differ sharply; missed appointments are measured in one shared system.
Decision: Let each site choose message timing and channel while retaining the shared outcome fields.
Reasoning: The same measurement backbone supports different judgments about implementation variance.

Situation: A retailer is changing return procedures across urban and rural stores.
Shared facts [history-03-02-fact]: Courier pickup is frequent in cities and weekly in rural areas; fraud checks use a common account service.
Message excerpt: Allow rural stores a longer physical-return window within the common fraud rules.

Situation: A school network is choosing lesson pacing for a shared science module.
Shared facts [history-03-03-fact]: Class schedules and prior knowledge vary; every class takes the same end assessment.
Retrospective: Give teachers a two-week pacing range and require a short local rationale.

Situation: A hospital group is defining shift handoff notes.
Shared facts [history-03-04-fact]: Specialties need different clinical detail; two recent incidents involved missing allergy and escalation fields.
log.decision=Mandate the safety fields and let specialties design the remaining note.

Situation: A franchise is deciding how stores should respond to local heat alerts.
Shared facts [history-03-05-fact]: Exposure and staffing differ by location; the insurer requires common incident reporting.
Decision: Let local managers adjust hours against published heat thresholds.

Situation: A payroll process must implement a new national withholding rule.
Shared facts [history-03-06-fact]: The effective date and calculation are statutory and identical for all offices.
Message excerpt: Deploy the same validated calculation in every office by the legal deadline.

Situation: An emergency alert contains a mandatory evacuation order.
Shared facts [history-03-07-fact]: The order and geographic boundary are issued by the authorized agency; local edits could change who receives it.
Retrospective: Distribute the authorized order unchanged through every local channel.

Situation: A library network is deciding whether branches can rearrange children's collections.
Shared facts [history-03-08-fact]: Branch usage differs; interlibrary requests rely on shared catalog codes; accessibility paths must remain clear.
log.decision=Allow branch layouts to vary while preserving catalog and accessibility constraints.

target_b.content:
Situation: A food bank is redesigning appointment reminders across four neighborhoods.
Shared facts [history-03-01-fact]: Language mix and phone access differ sharply; missed appointments are measured in one shared system.
Decision: Use one reminder sequence everywhere so site comparisons remain interpretable.
Reasoning: The same measurement backbone supports different judgments about implementation variance.

Situation: A retailer is changing return procedures across urban and rural stores.
Shared facts [history-03-02-fact]: Courier pickup is frequent in cities and weekly in rural areas; fraud checks use a common account service.
Message excerpt: Keep one return window and add centrally funded courier pickups to rural stores.

Situation: A school network is choosing lesson pacing for a shared science module.
Shared facts [history-03-03-fact]: Class schedules and prior knowledge vary; every class takes the same end assessment.
Retrospective: Use the common weekly sequence and provide centrally designed catch-up sessions.

Situation: A hospital group is defining shift handoff notes.
Shared facts [history-03-04-fact]: Specialties need different clinical detail; two recent incidents involved missing allergy and escalation fields.
log.decision=Adopt one group-wide handoff template and review specialty exceptions quarterly.

Situation: A franchise is deciding how stores should respond to local heat alerts.
Shared facts [history-03-05-fact]: Exposure and staffing differ by location; the insurer requires common incident reporting.
Decision: Use centrally issued hour changes for every store in an affected alert zone.

Situation: A payroll process must implement a new national withholding rule.
Shared facts [history-03-06-fact]: The effective date and calculation are statutory and identical for all offices.
Message excerpt: Deploy the same validated calculation in every office by the legal deadline.

Situation: An emergency alert contains a mandatory evacuation order.
Shared facts [history-03-07-fact]: The order and geographic boundary are issued by the authorized agency; local edits could change who receives it.
Retrospective: Distribute the authorized order unchanged through every local channel.

Situation: A library network is deciding whether branches can rearrange children's collections.
Shared facts [history-03-08-fact]: Branch usage differs; interlibrary requests rely on shared catalog codes; accessibility paths must remain clear.
log.decision=Use one layout standard so families and rotating staff can navigate every branch consistently.
